item.title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Andrew, Sam Hughes, Motiejus Valiunas

item.title: On Finite Groups with Element Order Set of Width 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.29004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite groups in which every element order is divisible by at most three distinct primes. We determine the possible nonabelian composition factors, prove that a nonabelian simple group with this property has at most $15$ prime divisors in its order, and deduce that $\rho(G)\leq192$ for every finite group $G$ with $\alpha(G)\leq3$.
item.dc:creator: Eric Min, Chloe So, Yong Yang, Eddy Zhang, Mengtian Zhang, Cody Zhou

item.title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $\beta_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].
item.dc:creator: Miguel Donoso-Echenique, Eduardo Silva

item.title: Kobayashi's problem for power semigroups of inverse semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a semigroup $S$ (written multiplicatively), let $\mathcal P(S)$ denote the semigroup of all non-empty subsets of $S$ under setwise multiplication. The finitary power semigroup $\mathcal P_\text{fin}(S)$ is the subsemigroup of $\mathcal P(S)$ consisting of all non-empty finite subsets of $S$. Kobayashi's problem asks for which classes $\mathcal O$ of semigroups every isomorphism $\mathcal P(H) \to \mathcal P(K)$ with $H, K \in \mathcal O$ maps singletons bijectively onto singletons and hence induces an isomorphism $H \to K$. We give an affirmative answer for inverse semigroups, extending previous results for groups, semilattices, and, more generally, Clifford semigroups. We also establish the corresponding rigidity theorem for finitary power semigroups. To this end, we develop a new framework that provides a common approach to both settings.
item.dc:creator: Shuolin Liu, Salvatore Tringali

item.title: The Conjugacy Problem for Recursively Presented Virtually Soluble Groups of Finite Pr\"ufer Rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.29563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve a long-standing conjugacy problem for finitely presented soluble groups of finite Pr\"ufer rank, recorded as Problem~9.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, in the stronger setting of recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble groups. Robinson proved that, in every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble minimax group, conjugacy to any fixed element is decidable, while explicitly lefting open whether the procedure could be made uniform in the target element. We establish this uniformity. More specifically, we prove that every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble group of finite Pr\"ufer rank has decidable Conjugacy Problem.
item.dc:creator: M. Brescia, E. Ingrosso, M. Trombetti

item.title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.29712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.
item.dc:creator: Friedrich Martin Schneider

item.title: The Diophantine Problem with constraints in some free-by-cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we explore the Diophantine Problem, that is, the solvability of equations, in one-relator and free-by-cyclic groups, showing that this is decidable in some cases and undecidable otherwise, depending on their abelianisation and centre. In particular, we focus on a version of the Diophantine Problem which asks about the existence of solutions satisfying abelianisation constraints, and prove a number of results concerning the decidability of this problem for free-by-cyclic groups with centre, tree-GBS groups, cyclically pinched groups and the first hydra group.
item.dc:creator: Laura Ciobanu, Robert D. Gray, Alex Levine

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Brieussel, Hanna Oppelmayer

item.title: Restriction of $p'$-degree characters, fields of values, and relative normal complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.29672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group for a prime $p$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Centella and Navarro proved that there is a canonical bijection ${\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_G})\to{\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_{\textbf N_G(P)}})$ preserving fields of values, where $\Phi_{1_G}$ denotes the principal projective indecomposable character of $G$. In the spirit of a result of Berkovich on the McKay bijection, we characterize when this projective correspondence can be realized by restriction, proving that it holds if and only if $\mathbf{N}_G(P)$ admits a certain relative normal complement in $G$. More generally, we establish a refined criterion incorporating fields of values, and we extend this characterization to $\pi$-separable groups with nilpotent Hall $\pi$-subgroups.
item.dc:creator: David Cabrera-Berenguer

item.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
item.description: arXiv:2411.00739v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma_p$ denote the Hecke group where $p=2r$, $r>0$. Let $\mathcal{N}_l$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements of word length $l$ in $\Gamma_p$. We prove that for $l \to \infty$, $$|\mathcal{N}_l| = \mathcal{O}\left(\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor^{s-1} \rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor} \right), $$ where $\mathcal O$ is the `big O', $\rho \in [\sqrt{2}, 2]$ is the unique positive real root of $$ p(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{j=1}^{r-1} x^{r-j} - 1, $$ and $s$ is the maximal multiplicity among the roots of $p(x)$. Our method relies on the free product structure of the Hecke group $\Gamma_p$, a combinatorial counting function, and recurrence relations derived from cyclically reduced representatives. We also derive that the growth rate of the primitive reciprocal classes of word length $l$ is in agreement with that of $\mathcal{N}_l$. This work generalizes previous results for odd $p$ and provides an explicit asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.
item.dc:creator: Debattam Das, Krishnendu Gongopadhyay

item.title: Cobordism, spin structures, and profinite completions
item.description: arXiv:2601.05706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth closed connected aspherical manifolds with good (in the sense of Serre) fundamental groups $G$ and $H$. We show that if $\widehat G\cong \widehat H$, then $M$ and $N$ are cobordant and the signatures of $M$ and $N$ agree modulo $8$. Moreover, $M$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$) if and only if $N$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$). We consider some analogous results for compact connected aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Andrew Ng

item.title: Regularity of Manhattan manifolds and exact dimensionality for relatively Anosov groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.13730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish several results about Patterson--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups. First, we prove that these measures are exact dimensional with respect to visual metrics induced by Gromov models in the Groves--Manning quasi-isometry class. Under the additional assumption that the group is relatively Morse, we show that the associated scalar Cartan metric is Gromov hyperbolic and that the corresponding boundary premetric is a visual metric to which the exact-dimensionality theorem applies. Second, we prove that their Manhattan manifolds are $C^1$-regular, from which we deduce that the growth indicator is $C^1$-regular and strictly concave on the interior of the limit cone. This extends the case of Anosov representations by Kim--Oh--Wang. Our methods are dynamical, and we exploit the fact due to Kim--Oh and Blayac--Canary--Zhu--Zimmer that Bowen--Margulis--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups are finite and mixing.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Reyes, Tianqi Wang

item.title: Near-Rings and Skew Braces
item.description: arXiv:2608.04874v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a deeper analysis of Rump's correspondence between near-rings and skew braces. We show that, under a topological assumption on the structure of a near-ring, Rump's correspondence is invertible and it is always possible to construct an associated skew brace. Furthermore, we provide several examples where this topological assumption is fulfilled in well-known algebraic structures such as the Nottingham group, groups of triangular functions, iterated wreath products of arbitrary groups, and groups of IA-automorphisms of free nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Aragona, Norberto Gavioli, Martina Iannaccone, Giuseppe Nozzi

item.title: Solubility from a disconnected common-divisor graph on $p$-regular conjugacy-class sizes
item.description: arXiv:2609.27960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime. We prove that if the common-divisor graph on the nontrivial conjugacy-class sizes of $p$-regular elements of $G$ is disconnected, then $G$ is soluble. This settles the remaining case identified by Camina and collaborators. Their structure results provide an abelian normal $p'$-subgroup $M$. We choose a noncentral $r$-element $x\in M$, with $r\ne p$, such that $[G:C_G(x)]$ is coprime to $pr$, and show that $C_G(x)/M$ is a $\{p,r\}$-group. Thus $C_G(x)/M$ is a Hall $\{p,r\}$-subgroup of $G/M$. The separation between the two graph components then implies that every $p$-regular conjugacy-class size in $G/M$ has all its prime divisors in $\{p,r\}$. A theorem of Dolfi and Lucido, together with Burnside's $p^a q^b$-theorem, yields the solubility of $G/M$ and hence of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Lin Zhang

item.title: Self measurable embeddings of mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a finite-type orientable surface without boundary, outside of a few low-complexity surfaces, we show that any measurable embedding of the associated mapping class group into itself is a measure equivalence. This is a measure-theoretic analog to the result of Ivanov and McCarthy that mapping class groups are co-Hopfian.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Gurieva

item.title: Global shadow estimates and Hausdorff measure criteria in higher rank
item.description: arXiv:2606.19779v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Patterson--Sullivan measures encode the distribution of orbits of discrete group actions near the boundary. We prove a global shadow lemma for Patterson--Sullivan measures associated to relatively Morse subgroups of higher-rank semisimple Lie groups. The estimate is uniform for shadows centered at arbitrary points in a Gromov model, including points deep in the cuspidal part, and expresses the contribution of each cusp in terms of peripheral growth. This extends the global shadow lemma of Stratmann--Velani for geometrically finite real hyperbolic groups. As applications, we establish local doubling and reverse doubling. Under Zariski density, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for Patterson--Sullivan measures to agree with the associated Hausdorff measures and to be Ahlfors regular. For symmetric linear forms, these criteria hold without Zariski density. We verify the criteria explicitly for cusped Hitchin representations and real-hyperbolic self-joinings.
item.dc:creator: Dongryul M. Kim, Hee Oh

item.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.26873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider the shifted truncations of the exponential series and their Galois groups: $$F_{n,a}(x) := \sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!}\qquad G_{n,a}:= \text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q}).$$ In this paper we prove that for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $G_{n,a}=S_n$ has natural density one, thus answering a question of Katz and Rivin.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Weinbaum
